title: Proper Scoring Rules: Log Loss & Brier Score
interviewAnswer: Proper scoring rules reward honest probabilistic forecasts: in expectation, reporting the true probability minimizes expected score. Log loss and Brier score are common examples.
why: Accuracy ignores how good probability estimates are.
intuition: Predictions of .51 and .99 can yield the same class decision but represent very different probability quality.
deepDive: Brier score is squared error on predicted probabilities; log score punishes assigning tiny probability to events that occur.
commonMistakes: Using accuracy to judge probability quality.
Assuming one proper score determines every thresholded decision.
production: Use proper scores for probability quality and separate cost-aware thresholds for decisions.
workedExample: Two classifiers with equal accuracy can have very different log loss because one is overconfident on mistakes.
